title: adder-subtractor
body:
The [[Combinational Logic|combinational]] circuit that does the arithmetic inside an
[[ALU]]. Built in three layers:

**Half adder.** Two input bits, two outputs. $S = A \oplus B$, $C = A \cdot B$. No carry
in, hence "half".

**Full adder.** Three inputs ($A$, $B$, $C_{in}$), two outputs:
$$S = A \oplus B \oplus C_{in} \qquad C_{out} = A \cdot B + C_{in}(A \oplus B)$$

**Ripple-carry adder.** $n$ full adders chained, each one's $C_{out}$ feeding the next
one's $C_{in}$. Simple, and slow: the carry has to propagate all the way from bit 0 to bit
$n-1$, so the delay grows with the word size. Faster designs (carry-lookahead) compute the
carries in parallel instead.

**Getting subtraction for free.** Two's complement means $A - B = A + \bar{B} + 1$, so one
XOR gate per bit plus a single control line $M$ does both operations:

- $M = 0$: each $B$ bit passes through unchanged, $C_{in} = 0$, so the circuit adds.
- $M = 1$: each $B$ bit is inverted, $C_{in} = 1$ supplies the $+1$, so the circuit
  subtracts.

That is why hardware needs no separate subtractor, and why two's complement won over the
other signed representations in [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]]. Overflow and carry out of the top
bit are what set the [[Status Bits]].
